title: Marigold Systems - joint listing & reference architecture harmonization
summary: Kickoff to align on Marigold's marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture choices for hybrid deployment, and joint solution packaging. Focus areas: VPC connectivity and private control plane, KMS compatibility, observability hooks, canary routing for model variants, and quantization trade-offs for edge appliances. Action items include a security pack, draft refarch diagram, and a short benchmark plan for RTP and throughput.
topics: Private deployment vs. Dedicated capacity for Marigold's customers
Canonical refarch diagram and runbook ownership
action_items: Alex - send Marketplace packaging checklist + draft commercial blurb by 2026-08-18
Priya - share sample refarch diagram (VPC + bastion + private control plane) by 2026-08-20
Jon - prepare quantization trade-off slides and expected perf delta for 8bit/4bit by 2026-08-24
Sofia (Marigold) - confirm KMS provider and ARN list by 2026-08-21
Tanya (Marigold) - run initial connectivity test to Redwood staging VPC and share results by 2026-08-22
next_steps: Redwood to upload security summary & SOC2 mapping doc
Schedule deep benchmark run (20k tokens across 3 models) week of Aug 31
Align on pilot acceptance criteria and telemetry dashboards
transcript:
Header: 2026-08-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Recording: automated
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jon Park (Redwood SA), Liam O'Rourke (Marigold Head of Platform), Sofia Alvarez (Marigold Sec Eng), Derek Holt (Marigold PM), Tanya Bhat (Marigold Cloud Ops)
---
[00:00] Alex: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. This is Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, with me is Priya our SE and Jon who is solutions. Um, quick goal for today, align on the listing reqs and the reference architecture for Marigold's joint solution — and surface any security blockers early.
[00:18] Liam: Yep, thanks Alex. Happy to be here. We, um, we're trying to get a 1.0 marketplace listing ready for Q4, and we need to confirm the hybrid deployment pattern for customers who want private control plane, and also the on-prem edge appliance variant.
[00:33] Priya: Great, can I ask a quick question — when you say private control plane, do you mean VPC peering or full air-gapped on-prem? There's a few options and that changes the packaging.
[00:42] Derek: Mostly VPC + optional on-prem appliance. A lot of our enterprise customers require a VPC-based control plane with KMS integration, and a small number will want an air-gapped box for sensitive sites.
[00:53] Jon: Okay so typical pattern is Redwood Private offering for VPC control plane, and a separate on-prem bundle that we can ship as a helm chart + doc runbook for air-gapped deployments. We'll need to confirm KMS/HSM compatibility for the latter.
[01:05] Sofia: On KMS — important for us to know whether Redwood can integrate with Azure Key Vault and an on-prem HSM (Thales). We also need audit log retention and a way to forward audit logs into our SIEM.
[01:18] Priya: Absolutely. Redwood supports common KMS providers, and we have an HSM integration guide. For audit logs we can stream to your syslog or S3 and provide an event schema for mapping. I'll follow up with the SOC2 section in our security pack.
[01:29] Liam: Great. Also curious about telemetry — we need per-route latency and per-token cost for customers. Is that surfaced in the listing dashboards?
[01:38] Alex: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-model and per-route latency, token breakdowns, and cost allocation. For marketplace listings we can add a sample dashboard link and a telemetry JSON schema.
[01:49] Tanya: For the on-prem appliance variant we care about quantization. We expect customers to run 4-bit quant on constrained hosts, but we need to understand the quality regressions and latency improvements.
[02:00] Jon: We'll prepare a quantization tradeoff slide deck showing expected throughput and a small eval set showing delta in quality. Quick note: quantization behavior changes with sequence length and batch size, so we'll include a matrix.
[02:10] Derek: Ballpark timeline question — if we start a pilot mid-August, can we have a marketplace beta listing by late September?
[02:18] Alex: That sounds feasible. Pilot -> security review -> certification -> listing. The gating items are security pack, runbook, and a short performance benchmark.
[02:25] Liam: Ok. Let's tee up the security review now. We need SOC2 mapping, SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, and a data residency statement.
[02:34] Priya: Quick run — SSO and RBAC are supported; we have an OIDC/SAML guide and support for SCIM for user sync. Data residency: hosted model is in regions we certify, Dedicated and Private let you pin to customer region. We'll include precise region names in the security pack.
[02:45] Sofia: Also need e-discovery and export controls for logs and transcripts — what's the retention policy?
[02:52] Alex: Default retention is 90 days for transcripts in hosted, configurable for Private and Dedicated. We can provide an SLA for retention and an export endpoint for audit.
[03:01] [crosstalk]
[03:05] Alex: On benchmarks — Priya, can you summarize what we'll propose for the joint pilot?
[03:09] Priya: Sure — propose a 3-model benchmark: one small-llm (LLM-small), one mid context model (open LLM-m), and a larger 16k variant. Run 20k tokens across each model, measure p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and throughput at 8, 16, 32 concurrency. We'll run in Redwood staging first and then on Marigold's staging VPC.
[03:27] Tanya: For the staging VPC test, we need connection instructions and a short SSH bastion doc. Can Redwood provide a temporary jump host?
[03:34] Jon: We can provide a temp reachable endpoint and a runbook. We'll also include security groups and expected egress rules.
[03:40] Derek: One objection — some customers are price-sensitive and will prefer a self-hosted gateway rather than paying for Dedicated. How do we position the economics?
[03:49] Alex: We'll bring Redwood Optimize recommendations — batching, prefix caching, and suggested quantization profiles. Our goal is to show unit economics for Dedicated vs self-host: often the difference is operational overhead plus telemetry and SLA. We'll prepare a short cost comparison slide.
[04:03] Liam: Competitors — we've talked to NimbusCloud earlier and they pushed a lock-in angle. We want to ensure the listing emphasizes portability and ability to pin model versions.
[04:12] Priya: Noted — we can include a portability note and sample API compatibility guidelines.
[04:16] [10:00 mark — mid-conversation, summarizing technical details]
[10:05] Priya: Important nuance — KV cache behavior for chat workloads. Our KV cache will live in the serving runtime; for Private deployments we expose a local cache option, and for Dedicated we maintain a distributed KV cache across pods. There can be warmup latency on first requests.
[10:22] Sofia: Is that cache encrypted at rest? We need encryption to the HSM keys.
[10:27] Jon: Cache is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and the encryption keys can be managed by your KMS provider. For HSM-backed keys we'll provide the necessary key wrap steps.
[10:38] Tanya: Any special networking requirements for the cache warmup? Large prefix loads could hammer the network.
[10:44] Priya: We'll recommend pre-warming and a seed cache strategy for those customers. We'll include configuration knobs in the runbook.
[10:54] Derek: On the listing - what artifacts will Redwood provide for the marketplace page?
[10:58] Alex: We'll provide a blurb, a reference architecture diagram, a short 'what customers get' list, sample SLAs, and a tile referencing the telemetry dashboard. Also a short one-pager on privacy and compliance.
[11:12] Liam: We should also include upgrade/rollback notes — customers will ask about canary deploys and automatic rollback policies.
[11:20] Jon: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model variants when quality drops. We'll share our rollout policy template.
[11:29] [15:00 mark — deeper security Q&A]
[15:04] Sofia: For auditability we need immutable event logs and a SHA-based chain for tamper evidence. Is that supported?
[15:12] Alex: We can provide append-only audit logs with push to your SIEM; tamper-evidence is achievable via signed logs. We'll include details in the security pack.
[15:22] Sofia: And what about redaction? Some customers want PII redaction on transcripts.
[15:28] Priya: We have post-processing hooks that can call a redaction lambda before storing transcripts. We'll share examples.
[15:34] Liam: Ok, moving to packaging for the on-prem appliance — what does the deliverable look like? Helm chart + docs? Container images?
[15:43] Jon: Helm chart + OCI bundle containing the runtime images and a compatibility matrix for supported kernels. We'll also include a quant profiles folder with pre-defined config for 8bit and 4bit.
[15:54] Tanya: Regarding the quant profiles, do you have a recommended CPU-only fallback? Some of our appliances are CPU-heavy.
[15:59] Priya: We do, but expect throughput to be much lower and latency higher. We'll include numbers in the slide deck. CPU-only is viable for very low TPS.
[16:08] Derek: For the joint solution, who owns the runbook and support for the marketplace customers? Is it Marigold support or Redwood?
[16:16] Alex: Typically joint customers will have a primary support owner defined in the listing. We can set a handoff: Redwood owns runtime issues and Marigold owns application-level triage, and both share an escalation path. We'll note this in the listing contract.
[16:27] Liam: Let's talk about the pilot success criteria — what are we measuring?
[16:31] Priya: Suggested criteria: p95 latency under X ms for model A, no critical security findings in the review, successful KMS integration (key wrap/un-wrap tested), and telemetry shows acceptable cost per 1k tokens. We'll align numbers once we pick models.
[16:46] [20:00 mark — logistics and scheduling]
[20:02] Alex: Next week we'll send the marketplace checklist and security pack. Can we schedule the benchmark week of Aug 31?
[20:09] Liam: That works for us, internal stakeholders are available then.
[20:12] Tanya: We'll need a short pre-run checklist from Redwood so we can open the right firewall rules.
[20:18] Jon: I'll add the firewall rules and a sample terraform snippet.
[20:23] Derek: One more operational note: billing meter expectations — some customers want per-conversation pricing, others per-token. Does the marketplace tile allow both?
[20:33] Alex: The marketplace supports multiple billing meter options; we'll include examples and recommended defaults. We'll also include a metering spec for the connector.
[20:40] [25:00 mark — brief demo pause, referenced deck link]
[25:05] Alex: I've dropped a link to the joint deck in chat — "redwood.com/marigold-deck-draft" (placeholder). Please don't circulate yet.
[25:12] Sofia: Saw it, looks good. One question on the deck slide about fallback policies — will Redwood run model A then model B automatically if model A fails?
[25:24] Priya: Yes, route policies allow primary/secondary model routing with automatic fallback and heuristics for quality checks.
[25:30] Liam: Sound good.
[25:33] [30:00 mark — edge case discussion]
[30:02] Tanya: Edge-case: offline inference — some sites have intermittent connectivity. How do you recommend handling sync and local KV stores?
[30:11] Jon: For intermittent sites we can recommend a local-only mode with periodic batch syncs. But you lose centralized telemetry; we'll flag that in the runbook and provide a local metrics exporter that caches events until connectivity returns.
[30:24] Derek: Will that local exporter be compatible with Prometheus?
[30:28] Priya: Yes, it's Prom-compatible and can push metrics when back online.
[30:33] [40:00 mark — wrap up and recaps]
[40:01] Alex: Quick recap of decisions: we agree on VPC-based private control plane + optional on-prem helm bundle; Redwood provides security pack, refarch diagram, quant trade-off slides, and runbook; Marigold to confirm KMS provider and run connectivity test.
[40:20] Liam: That matches our notes. We'll pull in legal for the platform listing agreement after the security pack.
[40:28] Sofia: Please include an item about retention and export in the pack.
[40:32] Alex: Will do. Any blockers that could stop the pilot?
[40:36] Tanya: KMS ARN confirmation and a clean networking test; those are prerequisites.
[40:41] Priya: We'll draft a minimal pre-flight checklist and attach it to the runbook.
[40:47] Derek: Ok, next steps and owners?
[40:50] Alex: I'll reconcile action items after this call. Jon will add firewall terraform, Priya will send refarch and quant slides, and Alex will send the marketplace checklist and security summary. Marigold owners will return KMS ARNs and run the connectivity test.
[41:07] [closing pleasantries]
[41:10] Liam: Thanks everyone. Excited to get this moving.
[41:14] Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the pack and schedule the benchmark. Bye.
[41:18] [end recording]
